description: Implement the immersive zoom transition and virtual safari scene. When a floating card is clicked, the camera zooms toward that globe point, the globe dissolves, and a full-screen parallax habitat scene emerges with scroll-based storytelling (comic strip panels, species data, threats). A 'return to globe' action reverses the transition.
steps: STEP 1 - Create src/safari-scene.js: This is the virtual safari module. It manages the full-screen habitat experience that appears after the zoom transition. Structure: (a) A class SafariScene with methods: enter(speciesSlug), exit(), and a private _render(data) method. (b) enter(slug): fetches species JSON from public/data/{slug}.json, builds the safari DOM inside #safari-container, enables Lenis smooth scroll for the safari content, triggers scroll-based GSAP animations for panels. (c) exit(): kills ScrollTrigger instances and Lenis, clears the container, hides it. (d) The safari DOM structure: a full-height parallax hero section at top with layered habitat scene (sky gradient, distant silhouette, mid-ground vegetation, species focal element, foreground elements - all as layered divs with parallax speeds), then below it scrollable content sections.

STEP 2 - Safari content sections rendered by _render(data): (a) Parallax habitat hero (100vh, layered gradients/silhouettes per biome type - use habitat.type to pick color palette), (b) Species intro card (name, scientific name, status badge, hero_stat, population info), (c) Comic strip panels section: generate 6 panels from species data combining habitat.description, threats, cultural_significance, conservation into a narrative arc: Panel 1 'In the Wild' (habitat snippet), Panel 2 'Ancient Bonds' (cultural_significance.mythology or first cultural_depth entry), Panel 3 'Under Threat' (first threat), Panel 4 'The Human Story' (cultural_depth entry or human-wildlife context), Panel 5 'Fighting Back' (conservation programs), Panel 6 'The Future' (population trend + what we can understand). Each panel has a title, narrative text, and source citation where available. (d) Threats section with visual cards for each threat. (e) On Screen section (TMDB media cards). (f) Cultural depth section. (g) Interesting facts. (h) References/sources.

STEP 3 - Implement the zoom transition in src/main.js (or a new src/globe-transitions.js): When a floating card is clicked: (a) Phase 1 (0-600ms): Clicked card highlights (scale up, glow), other cards fade to opacity 0. (b) Phase 2 (600-1400ms): Camera flies toward the species' 3D position on globe (use CinematicEngine.flyCamera to the point + normal offset so camera is looking at that spot from slightly above). Globe continues rendering. (c) Phase 3 (1400-2000ms): Globe group fades (opacity on materials or scene fog increase), #safari-container fades in (opacity 0 to 1), canvas z-index drops below safari. (d) Phase 4 (2000ms+): SafariScene.enter(slug) is called, Lenis scroll is enabled inside safari container. Use a single GSAP timeline orchestrating all phases.

STEP 4 - Implement 'Return to Globe' transition: A fixed button '.return-to-globe' appears during safari mode. On click: (a) SafariScene.exit() is called (scroll stops, content clears), (b) safari-container fades out, canvas z-index restores, (c) Globe materials fade back in, (d) Camera flies back to the default globe-viewing position (using flyCamera in reverse), (e) Floating cards fade back in. Duration ~1.5s total.

STEP 5 - Create src/safari-scene.css (or add to style.css): Styles for the safari experience: (a) #safari-container: position fixed, inset 0, z-index 20, overflow-y auto, background dark-to-habitat-gradient, opacity 0 pointer-events none by default, .active class makes it visible. (b) .safari-hero: height 100vh, position relative, overflow hidden, with child layers .safari-layer--sky, .safari-layer--far, .safari-layer--mid, .safari-layer--subject, .safari-layer--near each absolutely positioned with different parallax offsets. (c) .safari-content: relative, padding, max-width 800px centered. (d) .comic-panel: frosted glass card style, scroll-triggered reveal animation, with .comic-panel__label, .comic-panel__title, .comic-panel__text, .comic-panel__source. (e) .safari-species-intro: large centered card with species info. (f) .safari-threats-grid: grid of threat cards. (g) .safari-media-grid: film/documentary cards. (h) Color theming via CSS custom properties set based on habitat type (tropical-forest = greens, ocean = blues, arctic = icy blues, savanna = warm golds, etc.).

STEP 6 - Wire everything together in main.js: After CinematicEngine and Globe init complete and landing sequence finishes: (a) Create FloatingCards instance passing globe.speciesDataCache and a click callback, (b) In the render loop (engine.onUpdate), call floatingCards.update(camera) to reposition cards each frame, (c) The click callback creates a GSAP timeline for the zoom transition and calls safariScene.enter(slug), (d) The return-to-globe button calls the reverse transition and safariScene.exit().
acceptance_criteria: npm run build succeeds without errors
src/safari-scene.js exists and exports a SafariScene class with enter(slug) and exit() methods
The zoom transition is implemented as a GSAP timeline with the 4 phases described
Safari scene renders parallax habitat hero + comic strip panels + threats + media + cultural depth from species JSON data
A return-to-globe button exists and triggers reverse transition
Safari content uses Lenis smooth scrolling independently from globe state
